headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail minimal after Friday's record probe fully retraced into the close
body: Friday 2 October was the last session before the halt. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00%, after a softer September employment report showed 29,000 jobs added against about 90,000 expected and unemployment at 4.2%. The structurally important detail for this framework is that the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced into a close near the 30,737.07 session low. That is orderly mean reversion, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail stays at 3 for the whole window. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59%. Stress stays elevated at 57 and drifts modestly higher across the window on the carried-in environment rather than on observed structure: Treasury yields reversed upward despite the soft payroll print, with the 2-year at 4.84% and the 10-year at 5.28%, while Brent sits near $102.25, up 7.05% on the month and 58.45% on the year, with the Strait of Hormuz still not fully reopened. A fire and smoke plume was reported near an Aramco facility in Riyadh on Saturday amid escalating Saudi-Houthi exchanges; neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco had confirmed the incident or a cause at the time of this assessment, and no claim of responsibility had been made, so it is treated as an unresolved Stress and Confidence input rather than a priced supply shock. U.S. naval deployments continue, with the USS Theodore Roosevelt and the Makin Island amphibious group heading to the region. Confidence is 83: index level, session range, volatility, yields, oil and the seven-day calendar were all verified from primary sources, and the single open item is the unconfirmed cause of the Riyadh fire. No futures price discovery is available anywhere inside this forecast window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. The window opens inside Friday's post-payroll U.S. session with Tail 21-23 and Stress 76-79 under a mixed mode, then decays steadily after the 21:00Z futures close: Tail falls from 14 to 3 and Stress from 74 to 52 across the overnight and Saturday hours, with the mode settling to normal from 00:00Z. The final four hours sit flat at Tail 3 with Stress between 52 and 54.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this forecast window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no NQ price path can form and Tail is held flat at 3, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. Stress drifts from 57 to 62 purely because unresolved energy and Middle East threads accumulate without a market able to price them, and Confidence eases from 83 to 78 as Friday's verified levels age. The restart at 22:00Z on 4 October lies about six hours past the end of the final scored hour, so the first genuine post-weekend price-path evidence, and any restart gap, falls outside this horizon.
